# Diane Schrempp

Print Bio

## Veterinary Specialist

### DVM, DACVIM/Oncology

Dr. Diane Schrempp graduated from Kansas State University in 2007 with a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree. She then went on to complete a small animal rotating internship at Cornell University in 2008. In 2008 - 2009, Dr. Schrempp completed a one year oncology clinical trials internship at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Following that, she headed to Purdue University where she completed a three year comparative oncology residency. Dr. Schrempp became board certified through the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (Oncology) in 2012. She joined the team at VCA Veterinary Care Animal Hospital and Referral Center in Albuquerque, New Mexico in August 2012.

Her professional interests include diagnosing and treating a variety of canine and feline cancers, using new and cutting edge treatments for cancer (Palladia and metronomic chemotherapy) as well as applying a thorough knowledge of standard of care options (surgery and chemotherapy). She approaches cancer in a way that focuses on the patient's overall well-being and quality of life. When she's not taking care of cancer patients, Dr. Schrempp enjoys exploring her new home state with her West Highland White Terrier, Sam.

Cancer doesn’t affect companions the same way it affects humans. Understanding the differences helps guide better care.
Companions often show fewer early symptoms and can’t communicate discomfort, so signs may go unnoticed longer. The staff works tirelessly to provide the highest level of care, offering support, expertise, and reassurance through every stage of the journey. Cancer in companions is the uncontrolled growth of abnormal cells. It can affect different parts of the body and overall health.
Signs may include lumps, weight loss, appetite changes, or unusual behavior. Early detection is key to better outcomes.
Get expert care and support from Veterinary Cancer Care.

Chemotherapy for dogs and cats is designed with comfort in mind. Unlike human treatments, the goal is to maintain your pet’s quality of life, not push them to their limits.
Most companions experience little to no pain during treatment, and side effects are usually mild and manageable. Many continue to eat, play, and enjoy their normal routines.
Your veterinary team will adjust treatment as needed to keep your companion as comfortable as possible.

## Meet dr. Jeannette m. Kelly

Meet Our Full Team

Image: image

Dr. Jeannette M. Kelly founded Veterinary Cancer Care in 2004, recognizing that pets in New Mexico deserved access to specialized oncology care close to home.

A graduate of Colorado State University, Dr. Kelly completed a rigorous residency in veterinary oncology and became board-certified in 2009. Her approach blends the latest advances in cancer treatment, including immunotherapy, genomic testing, and clinical trials, with integrative therapies that support the whole patient.
They are legitimately concerned about the well-being of their patients and offer a holistic approach to veterinary medicine. They’ve provided top-notch care to our beloved lab.

 Dana H.

## frequently asked questions

Do I need a referral from my vet to schedule an appointment?

No. You can contact us directly to schedule a consultation. No referral required. We’ll coordinate with your primary veterinarian to ensure seamless care.

What happens during our first visit? 

We’ll review your pet’s medical history, Dr. Kelly will perform a comprehensive exam, and then we’ll discuss diagnostic recommendations and treatment options tailored to your pet. Treatment can begin the same day if you choose, but there’s never any pressure or obligation.

Do you treat all types of cancer? 

Yes. We diagnose and treat all forms of cancer in dogs and cats.

I live far away. Can I still come to your clinic? 

Absolutely. Many of our patients travel from across New Mexico and neighboring states. After your initial in-clinic consultation, we can coordinate follow-up care with your local veterinarian.

# Local Intralesional Chemotherapy Treatment for Pet Cancer

February 9, 2024June 26, 2019 by jerry

Veterinary oncologists have many tools at their disposal, but some we don’t hear much about. Local intralesional chemotherapy treatment for pet cancer is one of them.

Image: Santa Fe Vet Cancer CareInnovative pet cancer care treatment is found behind these doors.

This relatively affordable treatment can mean the difference between life and death for a Tripawd who develops a tumor in a remaining limb. We think everyone should know about it. Our friend Jeannette M. Kelly, DVM Diplomate ACVIM, Oncology, founder of the Veterinary Cancer Care clinic in Santa Fe, New Mexico, explains in the last of our interview series with her.

## All About Local Intralesional Chemotherapy for Pet Cancer

We first heard about Local Intralesional Chemo when Tripawds member Travis Ray was diagnosed with a soft-tissue sarcoma on a remaining limb.

An Integrative Approach to Cancer Care

## our philosophy

Image: image

At Veterinary Cancer Care, we believe healing requires more than treating a diagnosis. It requires treating the whole patient.

Dr. Kelly practices integrative veterinary oncology, combining the most advanced conventional treatments with holistic therapies that support your pet’s overall well-being. With access to genomic profiling, she can identify targeted therapies matched to your pet’s specific cancer cells. Treatment might also include pairing chemotherapy with nutritional supplements or using immunotherapy alongside herbal support. 
## our mission

At Veterinary Cancer Care, we believe that every pet deserves compassionate, expert oncology care that prioritizes quality of life.
Founded in 2004 by Dr. Kelly, our mission extends beyond treating cancer. We create a safe space where families receive the knowledge and support they need to make the best decisions for their pets.
Through innovative treatments that merge traditional and holistic approaches, we strive to make cancer care affordable and accessible, ensuring no family faces impossible choices due to cost.
We are committed to mentorship, nurturing the next generation of veterinary professionals, and fostering unity in our community. Our work is a testament to the belief that love is eternal, and through kindness, teamwork, and advocacy, we honor the unbreakable bond between people and their pets.
Veterinary Cancer Care is a place of healing, hope, and unwavering dedication to advancing oncology for the betterment of all.

SERVICE AREA

## Serving New Mexico and Beyond

We welcome patients from throughout New Mexico, including Santa Fe, Albuquerque, Taos, and Las Cruces, as well as families traveling from Texas, Arizona, Colorado, and California. After your initial consultation at our Santa Fe clinic, we coordinate ongoing care with your local veterinarian so distance is never a barrier to expert oncology support.
